source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:18 ('אעבדך — no pashta on the bet') + Minchat Shai on Gen 28:15 (the banked twin: 'the Michlol cites a Jerusalem manuscript with hataf qamatz on the root's first letter, and likewise I-WILL-SERVE-YOU of the seven years — a great anomaly; and the Chizkuni wrote the BET in hataf qamatz')
claim_en: THE WAGE-VERB AGAINST TWO ANOMALIES: אעבדך ('I will SERVE YOU seven years for Rachel,' 29:18) — the bet in plain qamatz (the long a), NOT the Chizkuni's hataf qamatz, and the root's first letter in the standard compound short e, NOT the Jerusalem manuscript's pointing that Minchat Shai calls a great anomaly; and exactly ONE pashta (the forward-leaning accent), on the final letter, none on the bet — his 29:18 ruling. The promise-verb twin banked at the Bethel unit lands here: SNAPSHOT sides with Minchat Shai at both stations.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:18 ('הקטנה — the nun dageshed')
claim_en: THE YOUNGER AS RULED: הקטנה ('Rachel your daughter, THE YOUNGER,' 29:18 — the wage's own object-clause) — nun with dagesh (the doubling dot) per Minchat Shai, letter-identical.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:17 ('ועיני לאה רכות — Ibn Ezra reports Ben Efraim reading it as lacking an aleph, meaning LONG; his master forgives him — he lacked nothing but wisdom: the word stands as written, and the sages read it as the LONG-ENDURING gifts — priesthood, Levites, kingship; Bereshit Rabbah: Leah great in her gifts') + Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 29:17 ('רכות — two: Leah's, and IF HE SPEAKS TO YOU SOFT WORDS')
claim_en: THE TENDER EYES STAND AS WRITTEN: רכות ('and Leah's eyes were TENDER,' 29:17) — the Torah's ONLY token of the word, written with no aleph: Ben Efraim's emendation (read it 'long') is refuted by the letter itself, and the enduring-gifts derash rides the word as written; the Kitzur's soft-words pair (Job's) is outside the Torah, named.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 29:17 ('ועיני at the head of a verse — three: Leah's tender eyes; and the EYES OF ISRAEL were heavy with age; and the eyes of the wicked shall fail — her eyes were tender fearing Esau, and Israel's eyes grew heavy seeing Jeroboam and Ahab in his line')
claim_en: THE TWO VERSE-INITIAL EYES: ועיני ('and the eyes of...') opens a verse exactly TWICE in the Torah — Leah's tender eyes (29:17) and Israel's age-heavy eyes (48:10, the man Leah's fear did not marry, blessing her rival's grandsons); the Kitzur's third, the failing eyes of the wicked, is Writings-side, named.
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the same wording at two seats, the Kitzur's reading at narrative strength)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:21 ('הבה את אשתי — end-stressed')
claim_en: THE DEMAND'S OWN STRESS: הבה ('GIVE my wife,' 29:21 — the Babel-imperative in one man's mouth) — end-stressed per Minchat Shai: the accent sits past the bet, on the final syllable; SNAPSHOT letter-identical.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:21 ('ואבואה — written FULL with vav, and all the rest in the Torah are lean')
claim_en: THE ONE FULL LET-ME-COME: ואבואה ('that I may COME to her,' 29:21) — written plene with the vav, the form's only full token in the Torah as Minchat Shai rules: the purpose-clause of the demanded wedding is the Torah's one full-spelled coming.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:25 ('זאת — the zayin dageshed')
claim_en: THE ACCUSATION'S HARD ZAYIN: זאת in 'what is THIS you have done to me' (29:25 — the deceived-accuser formula arriving in Jacob's mouth) — zayin with dagesh (the doubling dot) after the joined what-word, exactly per Minchat Shai.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:27 + 29:30 ('גם — the gimel with dagesh', both notes)
claim_en: THE ALSO OF THE SECOND BRIDE: גם in 'and he loved ALSO Rachel, more than Leah' (29:30) — gimel with dagesh (the doubling dot) and the maqqef (the joining stroke) binding it to its object, per Minchat Shai's twin notes here and at the counter-offer (29:27, likewise dageshed): the preference-formula's also-words are all hard.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:27 ('אשר — with galgal, not with maqqef')
claim_en: THE UNJOINED SERVICE-CLAUSE: אשר in 'for the service WHICH you will serve with me' (29:27) — Minchat Shai rules it accented, not maqqef-joined; SNAPSHOT agrees on the testable half: no maqqef, an accent on the word. The accent's IDENTITY is the gap: he names galgal (the rare wheel-accent) and SNAPSHOT stores munach (the common sustaining accent) — the galgal layer remains uninstrumented in the stream (standing gap, first probed instance).
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:28 ('וימלא — the lamed in tzere')
claim_en: THE FULFILLMENT AS RULED: וימלא ('and Jacob did so, and FULFILLED her week,' 29:28 — the compliance the machine popped on this root) — lamed dageshed in tzere (the long e) per Minchat Shai, letter-identical.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:28 ('את רחל בתו לו לאשה — in some books the word לו is absent; but in ALL the codices of Spain it is written, and so in the books of R. Meir and R. Gershom')
claim_en: THE SECOND TO-HIM STANDS: 29:28 carries לו ('to him') TWICE — 'and he gave TO HIM Rachel his daughter, TO HIM as wife': some books drop the second; the codices of Spain and the books of R. Meir and R. Gershom keep it, and SNAPSHOT keeps both — arbitrating with Spain. (The doubled to-him lands on the verse that finally pops the give-my-wife demand: the letter says twice whose wife she is.)
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

claim_en: THE CONTRACT IS DRAFTED PERFECTLY AND THE FRAUD GOES AROUND IT. Three specifications are read as deliberate anti-fraud terms - for RACHEL, YOUR DAUGHTER, THE YOUNGER - against three named swaps: not the other sister, not another woman of that name, no substitution by renaming, because the townsmen are deceivers. And then the switch defeats all three, not by breaching a term but by operating outside them: the substituted bride ANSWERED TO THE NAME all night. The pair is the sharpest case-file exhibit in the sweep - drafting law verse-perfect, and fraud in execution beating it anyway.

check.note: Anti-fraud contract terms shown to be defeated not by breach but by performance outside their scope.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: A STANDING LAW OF THE WEDDING CALENDAR IS BORN AT THIS VERSE. From 'complete the WEEK of this one' R. Yaakov bar Acha derives that ONE DOES NOT MIX ONE JOY WITH ANOTHER - the seven feast days must not be overlaid with a second celebration. A rule still governing the calendar, taken from a swindler's instruction for covering his own fraud.

check.note: A standing calendar law derived from an instruction given in the course of a deception.

middah: plain (complete-the-week read as one joy not mixed with another)

claim_en: THE DECEIT IS MIRRORED BACK AT THE DECEIVER IN HIS OWN WORDS. Called a deceiver in the morning, the substituted bride answers: is there a teacher without students? Did your father not call ESAU - and you answered him? The measure-for-measure is exact, and the chain is deliberate about it: the man who took a blessing by answering to a brother's name is taken by a woman answering to a sister's. The whole night is recorded, with the hints dropped all day and the lamps covered.

check.note: A deception repaid by the identical mechanism, stated by the victim as the reason it was permitted.

middah: E27 (the deceit answered in the deceiver's own words — a sister's name for a brother's)

claim_en: THE FRAUD IS FINANCED WITH THE VICTIMS' OWN COLLATERAL. The chain records the mechanics: the townsmen are convened, told the water has been blessed since this man came, and offered seven more years of him in exchange for silence; collateral is taken from them against disclosure - and the feast's wine, oil and meat are bought WITH THEIR PLEDGES. The name for the deceiver is then derived from this: he deceived his own townsmen, not only his son-in-law.

check.note: A fraud financed by pledges taken from the parties whose silence it buys, with the epithet derived from that fact.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: A DISPARAGING READING IS REBUKED IN THE CHAIN AND OVERRULED IN THE TRANSLATION. A public expositor who rendered her eyes WEAK was rebuked outright - your mother's eyes were weak - and the word re-read as tender from weeping, the tears being over a decree that assigned her to the wrong brother, which Rav Huna says her prayer then nullified. Onkelos does not soften the word but replaces the judgment: her eyes were BEAUTIFUL. Both members guard her honour, one by re-reading and one by re-rendering.

check.note: A pejorative reading rejected by rebuke in one member and by outright substitution in the other.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: THE TWO SISTERS ARE MADE A PARTITION TABLE OVER THE WHOLE OF LATER HISTORY. Chieftains against chieftains, kings against kings, lion-killers against lion-killers, prophets, judges, land-conquerors and land-dividers each matched; the override of the sabbath by offering on one side and by war on the other; and two nights of deliverance apportioned to each line. The elder is graded GREAT in gifts - an eternal priesthood and an eternal kingship - and the younger LESSER, her institutions temporary. A standing strategic table of the same kind as the tribe-against-kingdom table at gen_47.

check.note: Two figures made the axis of a matched partition of later history, with a permanence grading attached.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: A WORK-ETHIC RULE IS DERIVED FROM THE YEARS SERVED AFTER THE FRAUD. The way of the world is that a labourer works faithfully for two or three hours and then slackens; the claim here is that the LATTER seven years, served after the deception, were as complete and faithful as the first. R. Yochanan then reads the doubled service as a model for redemption: enslaved before the wife, enslaved after - so too enslaved before the redeemer's birth and after.

check.note: A work-ethic standard set by service rendered after the employer's proven fraud, then read as a redemption model.

middah: plain (the latter seven years as the work-ethic rule; the doubled service as a model, E10, beside)

claim_en: THE BLUNT DEMAND IS DEFENDED AS URGENCY AND RENDERED AS CONTRACT. The chain concedes the wording is coarse - even a dissolute man does not speak so - and defends it by the promise of twelve tribes and the speaker's age: I am eighty-four; if not now, when? Onkelos moves the other way and makes it contractual: the days of MY LABOUR are completed - term served, delivery due. Neither leaves the sentence as it stands.

check.note: A coarse demand defended as urgency by one member and converted into contractual language by the other.
